adjudication_records.issue_text: topics_controller.rb unsubscribe: TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id) can return nil for recipients who never visited the topic, causing NoMethodError and a 500; needs find_or_create_by

topics_controller.rb unsubscribe: current_user is nil for logged-out users clicking the email unsubscribe link, causing NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a login redirect; no authentication before_filter or anonymous guard

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action unconditionally uses `current_user` (`TopicView.new(..., current_user)` and `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`). The diff shows no login/authentication before_filter added for `:unsubscribe` and no guard for `current_user.nil?`, so a logged-out user hitting `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` would raise `NoMethodError` on `current_user.id` and 500 instead of redirecting to login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-route-map.js.es6: topicUnsubscribe route is unreachable because the topic resource's nested fromParamsNear child (/:nearPost) matches /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe first, treating 'unsubscribe' as a post number; route must be nested inside the topic resource or declared before the catch-all

adjudication.rationale: In `app-route-map.js.es6`, the potentially greedy route is `topic.fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost`, but it is nested under the `topic` resource whose base path is `/t/:id` (per the diff context). That route would match at most `/t/<id>/<nearPost>` and cannot fully match `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` because it would leave an extra `/unsubscribe` segment unmatched. Ember route matching requires the whole URL to be consumed by a route; leftover segments prevent a match. Therefore the new `topicUnsubscribe` route is not shown as unreachable by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Template placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs maps to route name 'topic.unsubscribe' but the declared route is top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' whose lookup is topic-unsubscribe.hbs, so the template is never resolved

adjudication.rationale: The Ember route added is top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`, and corresponding JS files are named `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, and `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, which implies the resolved template name should be `topic-unsubscribe` (i.e., `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`). However, the template added is at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which conventionally maps to the nested route/template `topic.unsubscribe` (`topic/unsubscribe`). No nested `topic` resource route (`this.resource('topic', ...)`) or `this.route('unsubscribe', ...)` under it is added in the diff, so this template path/name will not be found for `topicUnsubscribe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: message_builder.rb: I18n.t('unsubscribe_link') interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} which raises MissingInterpolationArgument for emails built with add_unsubscribe_link: true when opts lack unsubscribe_url; only send_notification_email passes it; should default the key in MessageBuilder#initialize

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `Email::MessageBuilder#initialize` only seeds `site_name`, `base_url`, and `user_preferences_url` into `@template_args` and then merges `@opts`—it does not provide a default `unsubscribe_url`. In `html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, it calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, which will raise `MissingInterpolationArgument` if `unsubscribe_url` is not present in `template_args`. The diff only shows `send_notification_email` (and its spec) being updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, so other `add_unsubscribe_link: true` call sites would now break unless they also pass it or MessageBuilder defaults it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe writes tu.notification_level via tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change, bypassing the MessageBus publish that syncs notification-level changes, leaving an open topic tab showing a stale notification level

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code updates `tu.notification_level` and persists via `tu.save!` (new method in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is the mechanism that publishes `MessageBus.publish(... notification_level_change ...)` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set (`app/models/topic_user.rb`). By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this new unsubscribe path will not emit the MessageBus event to the current user, so any already-open topic view relying on that event can remain out of sync with the new notification level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError for anonymous/logged-out visitors because TopicUser.find_by can return nil and notification_level is called without a nil guard; no login-required filter covers :unsubscribe

State mutation on unauthenticated, untokenized GET: unsubscribe mutates notification_level with no confirmation token or CSRF protection, so email-scanner prefetch can silently mute users' topics (or toggle levels on repeated fetches)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (new action) the route is exposed as a `get "t/:.../unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and it **mutates state** by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. Because this mutation happens on an untokenized GET, there is no CSRF protection (Rails CSRF is generally enforced on non-GET) and no confirmation token in the URL; any automatic link prefetch/email scanner or repeated fetch can silently change a user's topic notification state (it even toggles between `:regular` and `:muted` on subsequent requests). The diff also adds the unsubscribe URL into emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and `unsubscribe_link` text), increasing the likelihood of automated fetching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Changing unsubscribe_link locale template to require %{unsubscribe_url} breaks every other mailer using add_unsubscribe_link: true, since only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url; I18n interpolation raises MissingInterpolationArgument

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` without supplying a default `unsubscribe_url`; `template_args` only contains what callers pass via `@opts`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` in this diff is updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, so any other existing caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not add `unsubscribe_url` would raise `MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic#unsubscribe_url produces a relative link (no Discourse.base_url prefix), resulting in broken per-topic unsubscribe links in emails and List-Unsubscribe headers

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is defined as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` (app/models/topic.rb), and elsewhere the code demonstrates that `post.url` is relative and requires `Discourse.base_url` to form an absolute URL in emails (`notification.html.erb` uses `Discourse.base_url` + `post.url`). The mailer passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` into the email template args (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb), and the server locale string renders it directly into a Markdown link (config/locales/server.en.yml). Nothing in `Email::MessageBuilder` prefixes `unsubscribe_url` with `Discourse.base_url`, and the spec even supplies a relative `"/t/1234/unsubscribe"`. This makes the per-topic unsubscribe link in emails a relative href, which is plausibly broken in email clients (and similarly risky for any header using it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No MessageBus publish after direct tu.save! in unsubscribe action, so open topic views show stale notification level until reload

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code updates `TopicUser` by mutating `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` directly. Elsewhere in the diff (`TopicUser.change` and `update_last_read`) notification-level changes publish `MessageBus` events (`MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })`). Because `unsubscribe` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, no publish occurs, so any already-open clients relying on MessageBus for live notification level updates would not be notified and could display stale state until a reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing behavioral tests: no assertions that unsubscribe text/URL appears in email body, that the controller toggles notification levels, handles nil TopicUser, or works unauthenticated; only the List-Unsubscribe header spec is touched

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new, nontrivial behavior (email body now includes a per-topic unsubscribe link via `unsubscribe_url` passed into templates, and a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates `TopicUser.notification_level`). The only spec change shown is in `message_builder_spec.rb`, which just adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options; the finding is correct that there are no new assertions that the unsubscribe text/URL appears in the rendered email HTML, and there are no tests for the new controller action’s toggling behavior or edge cases (e.g., `TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil, and `current_user` being nil would break), none of which are covered in the diff’s tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Slug-mismatch redirect in unsubscribe re-enters the action and toggles notification_level twice (tracking→muted→tracking), leaving users with stale slug-less URLs still notified despite unsubscribing

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the slug-mismatch (or missing slug for non-JSON) branch does `return redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301` *before* any `TopicUser` lookup or `notification_level` mutation. The toggle logic runs only after passing that redirect check, so a request that gets redirected does not toggle once and then toggle again; it only toggles on the final (post-redirect) request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Global unsubscribe_link locale string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but message_builder.rb:67 passes I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) with no fallback, causing I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and failed email delivery for every existing mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url (e.g. signup/activation, digest, other UserNotifications emails)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it still does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` without providing any default `unsubscribe_url` in the base `@template_args` (only `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` are set). Therefore, any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` during email building. The diff only updates one mailer/spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, so the risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe in topics_controller.rb:98 lacks a current_user guard and anonymous handling, so logged-out users clicking the email link get a 500 instead of a login redirect

The diff shows no guard/redirect (e.g., `ensure_logged_in`) added for `unsubscribe`, and routes expose it via GET (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: render :show added inside perform_show_response in topics_controller.rb:500 changes the HTML response of the existing #show action, not just the new unsubscribe action, an unscoped behavioral change to the core topic-view path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `render :show` inside `perform_show_response`’s `format.html` block. `perform_show_response` is called by both `show` and the new `unsubscribe` action; for `show` the implicit/default HTML render would already be `show`, so making it explicit does not verifiably change the existing `#show` HTML response. The explicit render primarily ensures the new `unsubscribe` action (which also calls `perform_show_response`) renders the topic `show` template instead of attempting to render an `unsubscribe` server template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Large amounts of cosmetic reformatting (var→const, brace style, route reordering in routes.rb:437-440, whitespace/indent restructure) are interleaved with the functional change, obscuring the diff's true surface and complicating review, bisect, and revert

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly mixes functional additions (new unsubscribe route/controller/template/model methods and email unsubscribe_url plumbing) with unrelated cosmetic refactors: e.g. `topic-from-params.js` converts `var`/function syntax to `const`/method shorthand and rearranges declarations; `topic_user.rb` changes indentation, hashes, and compresses loops; `email/notification.html.erb` is reindented/reformatted; `lib/email/message_builder.rb` changes formatting/ternary layout; `config/routes.rb` reorders several topic routes around the new unsubscribe routes. These non-functional changes are interleaved with the feature work and do obscure review/bisect/revert without being a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET that is non-idempotent: the toggle logic sets regular then muted on refresh/prefetch, so page loads or email-link prefetchers silently change notification level

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes to `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb) and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe` that mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` with toggle-like logic (`if tu.notification_level > ... then regular else muted; tu.save!`). Because it is a state-changing GET and can flip state across repeated loads (e.g., watching/tracking -> regular, then a subsequent refresh regular -> muted), a normal page load/prefetch can silently change notification level. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for users who never loaded the topic (e.g. mentioned by email before visiting), causing NoMethodError and a 500 on unsubscribe

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately reads/writes `tu.notification_level` without checking `tu` for nil. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic (e.g., user clicks the new email-provided `unsubscribe_url` before ever visiting the topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and result in a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: notification_level is nullable, so tu.notification_level > regular raises NoMethodError on NULL-level rows

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then compares `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`. The `TopicUser` model in this diff explicitly treats `notification_level` as possibly NULL via `COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular)`, so `tu.notification_level` can be `nil`. In Ruby, `nil > integer` raises `NoMethodError`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe route crashes for anonymous users because email link targets a logged-in session with current_user nil; no login redirect or per-user unsubscribe token

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code dereferences `current_user` without any nil guard: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and especially `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`. If an anonymous user hits `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (e.g., from an email link opened while logged out), `current_user` will be `nil` and `current_user.id` will raise, causing a crash. The diff does not add any explicit login requirement or redirect/token mechanism for this route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client route map only declares the slug URL shape while server registers both slug and slugless routes, so slugless unsubscribe URLs fall through to unknown-route handling in SPA navigation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete mismatch: the Ember route map adds only `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` while Rails registers both `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`. However, the claim that slugless URLs definitively “fall through to unknown-route handling in SPA navigation” isn’t directly verifiable from this diff (it depends on how Discourse intercepts/handles in-app link navigation). It’s still a specific, diff-grounded concern that client/server route shapes are out of sync and could cause edge-case routing issues if `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` is ever navigated client-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shared unsubscribe_link locale string always interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, so mailers using add_unsubscribe_link: true without passing unsubscribe_url render the raw literal placeholder with a broken link

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` unconditionally, but `Email::MessageBuilder`’s default `@template_args` (lib/email/message_builder.rb) does not define `unsubscribe_url` unless the caller passes it via opts. This PR updates one caller (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) and one spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but the diff does not show whether other existing call sites use `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without providing `unsubscribe_url`. So the concern is real and diff-grounded as a backward-compatibility requirement, but an actual breakage cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe route mutates notification state on a GET request

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) and a `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates persisted state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. This is a state-changing operation performed via GET, which is a correctness/security issue (e.g., can be triggered by crawlers or CSRF-prone GET requests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id) raises NoMethodError when current_user is nil, returning a 500 for unauthenticated requests (e.g., email link prefetchers), instead of redirecting to login

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` with no guard for `current_user` being nil. If the unsubscribe URL is hit unauthenticated (e.g., email client prefetcher), `current_user.id` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of redirecting to login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-topic unsubscribe sentence was added to the shared unsubscribe_link locale, changing the footer of every email using add_unsubscribe_link, not just topic notification emails

The diff shows one caller updated to pass `unsubscribe_url` (and the spec updated accordingly), but the shared nature of the locale means broader scope/impact than just topic notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Other mailers using add_unsubscribe_link with html_override call I18n.t without unsubscribe_url, raising I18n::MissingInterpolationVariable so those emails fail to build and are not delivered

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, and `template_args` has no default `unsubscribe_url` (only `user_preferences_url`, etc.). The diff updates `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` and the spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but any remaining `add_unsubscribe_link` callers that aren’t updated would now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationVariable` during email build.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe toggle only demotes tracking/watching users to regular instead of muted, so they can still receive notifications despite the footer promising they will stop receiving notifications

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code toggles the user’s `TopicUser.notification_level` such that if it’s above `:regular` (e.g., tracking/watching), it is set to `:regular`, not `:muted`: ```rb if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] else tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted] end ``` But the new UI/email copy promises “You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}.” / “To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic…”. Setting to `:regular` can still allow topic-related notifications (at least user-directed ones), so the behavior does not match the promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET-based unsubscribe action mutates notification_level with no CSRF protection, allowing cross-site forced mute/untrack of any topic via embedded image tags; should be POST/token-authorized

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `GET` route `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) mapped to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. That action mutates server state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (no token/nonce shown). Because it is a GET endpoint, Rails’ CSRF protections typically won’t apply, and this can be triggered cross-site (e.g., via an embedded image/link) for any logged-in user, causing forced mute/regular toggling of a topic’s notification level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil-dereference 500 when no TopicUser row exists: find_by returns nil for topics the user never opened, and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError; also current_user is nil on anonymous-access sites

If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic (e.g., user clicks the new email topic-unsubscribe link without ever visiting the topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500. The finding’s claim about `current_user` being nil is less supported because `:unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`, but the nil-`tu` dereference is directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe action skips guardian topic-access checks and performs no additional authorization for the slug-mismatch redirect; TopicView may raise Discourse::InvalidAccess unhandled, causing a 500 instead of 403 and leaking topic existence information

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe endpoint performs destructive, state-mutating data change (rewriting topic_users.notification_level and saving) on an unauthenticated-by-token HTTP GET with no confirmation or rollback, and email prefetchers like Gmail/Outlook scanners can auto-trigger it, destroying notification preferences with no backup of the prior value

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topics#unsubscribe` action that is routed via HTTP GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, it mutates persisted state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. There is no confirmation step in the controller/view flow; the action immediately toggles between `:regular` and `:muted`. This is a real correctness/security issue because GET requests should not perform state changes and can be triggered unintentionally (e.g., link scanners/prefetchers), leading to unintended notification preference changes with no rollback/previous-state preservation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:) returns nil for users with no TopicUser row, causing tu.notification_level to raise NoMethodError and return a 500 on the feature's primary entry point; TopicUser.change should be used instead

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences it (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`) with no nil-check. From the diff alone, there is no guarantee a `TopicUser` row exists for every `(current_user, topic)` pair, so `find_by` can return `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` and a 500 on the unsubscribe route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Toggle semantics silently destroy the user's actual prior state: a user at tracking is dropped to regular (still receiving notifications, contrary to the email's promise) while a regular user is demoted to muted, and repeated visits can flip levels with no record of the original setting

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` with a lossy toggle: if `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` it is forced down to `:regular`, otherwise it is set to `:muted` (`app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). This means users who were `:tracking`/`:watching` are not actually “stopped” from topic notifications as the UI/email text claims (they’re left at `:regular`), and a subsequent visit can further change `:regular` to `:muted`, irreversibly discarding the original higher level. This matches the finding’s claim about silently destroying prior state and inconsistent semantics with the unsubscribe promise added in locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe link embeds the topic's canonical slug URL, so slug renames cause 301 redirects that re-trigger the destructive GET, and with no token or expiry, archived emails remain live triggers for the data destruction

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` endpoint (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`) that flips `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves it, with no token/expiry or CSRF protection shown. The unsubscribe URL embedded in emails is `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` (mailer) which is built from `Topic#url` + `/unsubscribe` (includes the canonical slug). If the slug later changes, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` will 301 redirect when `slugs_do_not_match` to the new canonical `unsubscribe_url`, and the follow-up GET performs the notification-level change. So archived email links remain valid triggers for a destructive GET, and slug changes add an extra redirect hop before the mutation occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by in unsubscribe returns nil for users with no existing TopicUser row, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and a raw 500 instead of a 4xx or 'already unsubscribed' response

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and assigns to `tu.notification_level` before `tu.save!`. If `find_by` returns `nil` (no existing `TopicUser` row), this will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500. The diff shows no guard or fallback creation path (e.g., `TopicUser.change` / `find_or_create_by`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET with no confirmation or token, so email scanner prefetchers or link previews can permanently mute the topic without CSRF protection

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicsController#unsubscribe` and routes it via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb). That action mutates state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb) without any confirmation or token, and it’s linked directly from emails via `unsubscribe_url` (user_notifications.rb + Topic#unsubscribe_url + server.en.yml). Because it’s a GET endpoint that changes user state, it can be triggered by link prefetchers/scanners or previews and lacks CSRF-style protection/intent verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller mutates tu.notification_level via tu.save! directly, bypassing TopicUser.change which publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus message, leaving other tabs showing stale 'watching' state

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff updates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly (new code in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`), instead of using `TopicUser.change(...)`. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is responsible for publishing `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` when `notification_level` changes (`app/models/topic_user.rb`). By bypassing it, this unsubscribe toggle won’t emit the notification-level change event, so any real-time UI that relies on that MessageBus message (e.g., other open tabs) can remain stale until reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 route has no error action, so if PostStream.loadTopicView rejects (deleted topic or lacking permission), user gets generic Ember error route with no message tied to the unsubscribe link

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` and the route defines only `didTransition` in `actions`, with no `error` action / rejection handling. From the diff alone, a rejection (e.g., 404/403 from `loadTopicView`) would fall back to Ember’s default error handling rather than a custom message/flow for the unsubscribe page. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/UX gap, but not a clearly verifiable functional defect beyond default error routing behavior.
